1a.text: One input changes. Now your AI agent has to work out what that broke.

1c.text: Re-read everything. Accurate, but you pay for every token, every time.

1d.text: Or search for what looks related. Cheap, but blind to what matters.

loudness.type: linear gain 2.35 dB + peak limit -2 dBFS (4x oversampled)

2a.text: Agents build reports on their own earlier work, so every number quietly depends on inputs underneath.

2b.text: Correct one exchange rate, and some of those numbers are now wrong.

2c.text: But a total can depend on that rate without ever mentioning it.

2d.text: Similar words are not the same as real dependencies.

loudness.type: linear gain 1.40 dB + peak limit -2 dBFS (4x oversampled)

3a.text: ProofFlow is a context layer that follows structure instead of guessing.

3b.text: Every number keeps its receipts: exactly which inputs, and which tool, made it.

3c.text: So when something changes, the agent gets exactly what broke. Nothing more.

loudness.type: linear gain 2.79 dB + peak limit -2 dBFS (4x oversampled)

4a.text: An input, like the exchange rate, is saved as a version.

4b.text: A tool reads it, and leaves a receipt.

4c.text: The receipt points to its result, and each number in a report points to that result.

4e.text: The change travels up those links. Both revenue figures are withheld, never shown stale.

4f.text: Support never read the rate, so it stays current, and is reused.

4g.text: Refresh re-runs only the affected steps.

loudness.type: linear gain 3.56 dB + peak limit -2 dBFS (4x oversampled)

5b.text: Upload orders as a CSV, preview them, and create two reports.

5c.text: Publish a corrected rate. Affected figures are withheld, and the graph shows exactly why.

5d.text: Refresh brings them current. A checked report can only be copied while every figure is current.

5e.text: Agents get the same workflow through MCP. Six tools, one download.

loudness.type: linear gain 1.59 dB + peak limit -2 dBFS (4x oversampled)

6a.text: Under the hood, it's small, and strict.

6b.text: At the center is the runtime. Every tool run produces an immutable result, and a receipt.

6c.text: Content goes into a store that verifies every hash.

6d.text: Relationships go into HydraDB, as a lineage graph.

6e.text: When a correction arrives, HydraDB walks that graph natively, to find everything downstream.

6f.text: That walk becomes the agent's context. Traverse the structure. Skip the re-read.

6g.text: The runtime re-runs stale steps in order, reuses what's current, and records new receipts.

6h.text: If evidence is missing, it fails closed. No fallback. No guess.

6i.text: Agents reach it through a browser app, a Python API, or an MCP server, choosing plans from typed tools, never arbitrary code.

loudness.type: linear gain 3.53 dB + peak limit -2 dBFS (4x oversampled)

7a.text: So how does it compare to today's approaches?

7b.text: We froze one study. Forty-eight real model calls, the same task for every method.

7c.text: Re-reading everything got all thirty-two reports right, for three dollars seventy-four.

7d.text: ProofFlow also got thirty-two of thirty-two, with a hundred forty-two thousand fewer input tokens, for a dollar thirty-eight. Sixty-three percent less.

7e.text: Vector search cost the same as ProofFlow, and got five right. Keyword search, twenty-five. Hybrid, twenty-eight.

7f.text: On a separate retail benchmark, thirty-eight of thirty-eight, with sixty-nine percent fewer evidence tokens.

7g.text: A plain dependency walk over the same links ties it. The win is recording the structure.

loudness.type: linear gain 1.36 dB + peak limit -2 dBFS (4x oversampled)

8c.text: Built for teams whose agents produce numbers people act on: finance, revenue, analytics. Add it to any agent through MCP.

8d.text: Try it live. Every number shown is in the public evidence.
